summary: The galaxy war is three wars fought at once (sides.js:29-57) over 16 war systems: every system that has a planet, minus Dagobah. They are joined by 28 adjacency edges (gcw.js:90-112; I dumped the graph). It runs on a 72 h wall-clock campaign of 360 twelve-minute steps (gcw.js:51-75). history() (gcw.js:239-326) is a pure, seeded replay from each war's opening map. The AI is very simple. The liberator works the 4 worthiest fronts at a rate fixed per system for the whole campaign, drawn from [-2,12] %/h, or [-3,6] for worth >= 2 (gcw.js:200-208, 219-220). The raider launches one weight-random attack every 4 h (Hoth weight 4), lasting 1.6 h at 30-75 %/h (gcw.js:223-237, 267-270). The Hutts raid every 12 h (gcw.js:271-274). There is no defence, no regeneration, no counter-attack, no reaction to losses, no momentum or underdog effect, and no supply connectivity: supplyOf is a ±0.5 %/h neighbour count (gcw.js:176-180). The only shared state is the tally (pointsKey/winKey). Player points apply at any system with no cap beyond CAP=60 (warState.js:27). I simulated history() step by step in Node using an instrumented copy that I checked against the real module. With nobody playing (60 campaigns per war), about 8 systems change hands per campaign, the first change comes about 12 h in (5-34 h), and the longest quiet spell averages about 20 h (max 58.6 h). The major order is stuck (AI rate <= 0.5 %/h) about 41% of the time, and never changes all campaign in 6-10 of 60. In the Civil War it always opens on Coruscant, and its rate is negative in 15 of 60. Raider attacks succeed 19-27% of the time, and the 24-29% aimed at Hutt worlds succeed 3%. Hutt raids succeed 5-7%. The Remnant is eliminated in 6 of 60 campaigns (as early as 24 h) and the Hutts in 14 of 60. Outcomes are seed luck. The campaign then resets at 72 h with no result shown. With a single pilot the war is decided by that one person. Playing 3 h a day at 15 points plus a win per battle, they end the war outright in 13-26 of 30 campaigns; the Remnant is wiped out as early as 19 h. Grinding all day ends every war in 7-15 h. The holotable (HoloMap.jsx) shows ownership only as a 2 px ring round each system's dot. It shows a progress arc whose colours are hard-coded to the Civil War, so the Clone Wars and Remnant War maps are wrong (galaxy.css:531-532, 560-561). It draws the 6 trade routes but not the 28 edges the war actually uses (18 are invisible), and has a one-line legend, a war card (major order bar, battles list, area lines, rank and record) and war tabs that change your fighting theatre. There is no territory shading, no front lines, no fleets or arrows, no per-faction strength, trend or event log, no campaign result and no emblems. mine() costs 424 ms with 40 wins and is recomputed every second by HoloMap. I prototyped a deterministic AI v2 in the scratchpad (gcw_proto.js) with campaign phases, front rates re-rolled every 6 h, holder defence and regeneration, a captured system held at 0.7, target choice by utility per faction doctrine, counter-attacks, front rotation when stalled, supply connectivity, an underdog boost, a last stand and a climax. Over 40 campaigns per war with nobody playing it gives balanced outcomes (Civil War 7.2/6.1/2.8 systems, Clone Wars 7.0/6.8/2.1, Remnant 9.1/5.3/1.6), no elimination or early end before 66 h, about 30 changes per campaign, and a major order stuck at most 13% of the time (0-1% in the tuned pass). A pilot playing 3 h a day shifts the result by about 4-5 systems, but no war ends before the climax (66 h). Full replay cost is 54 ms against 15 ms now, so it needs caching.

rootCauses.title: Front rates are fixed for the whole campaign, so the headline objective stalls for days
rootCauses.mechanism: campaignPlan draws one rate per system per campaign from [-2,12] (worth >= 2: [-3,6]). frontsOf always takes the worthiest bordering systems first, and the major order is fronts[0]. A negative or near-zero rate on the worthiest front therefore holds the major-order slot until the end; there is no rotation or stalemate breaker.
rootCauses.evidence: gcw.js:206, 219-220, 325. Simulated, nobody playing, 60 campaigns per war: the major order is stuck (effective AI rate <= 0.5 %/h) 41% (Clone Wars), 43% (Civil War) and 37% (Remnant War) of steps. Its tenure averages 14.7 / 18.8 / 16.4 h, max 72 h. It never changes all campaign in 10 / 8 / 6 of 60. The Civil War's opening major order is Coruscant in 60/60 campaigns and the Remnant War's is Scarif in 60/60, with the opening major's own rate below 0 in 15/60 and 16/60. Clone c1 trace: Yavin held the major for 13.4 h at -2.3 %/h.

rootCauses.title: No defence, regeneration or reaction: holds only ever fall, and a dented system stays dented
rootCauses.mechanism: control only goes down, except from the owner's player points, an attack timing out (back to 1) or a capture (back to 1). A front that drops out of the top 4 keeps its damage for the rest of the campaign. A Hutt raid at 20-45 %/h × 1.6 h (32-72%) then finishes it: the Hutts gain worlds by accident.
rootCauses.evidence: gcw.js:289 (Math.min(1, control - fall), no regeneration term), 294, 298-303. Clone c1 trace: Hoth went Separatists → Hutts at 13.4 h after a Republic front had cut it to 0.28 and a 21.7 %/h raid finished it. Naboo went the same way at 49.6 h (0.59 → raid).

rootCauses.title: Raider and Hutt targets are weight-random, so many operations are futile
rootCauses.mechanism: attackOn picks a border system at random weighted by `weight` (Hoth 4), with no regard to worth, how damaged it is, supply, or whether the attack could succeed. Hutt worlds feel only half of any rate (pressureOn), so an attack on one can't take more than 0.5×75×1.6 = 60% of its hold, yet the raider keeps attacking them. Only one raider attack runs at a time, on a fixed 4 h clock, with no counter-attack after a loss.
rootCauses.evidence: gcw.js:197, 223-237, 267-270; systems.js:217 (Hoth weight 4). Simulated, nobody playing: raider attacks succeed 19% (Clone Wars), 24% (Civil War), 27% (Remnant War). Of them, 29% / 24% / 9% target Hutt worlds and succeed 3% / 3% / 8%. Hutt raids succeed 7% / 6% / 5%. Clone c1 trace: the Separatists attacked Hutt-held Hoth 7 times, at 24, 28, 32, 36, 44, 48 and 56 h, and failed every time.

rootCauses.title: The pace is glacial and lumpy, then the campaign resets with no result
rootCauses.mechanism: With nobody playing, fronts move 2-12 %/h, so a system takes 8-50 h. The first raider attack is at 4 h. Over 72 h only about 8 systems change hands. At 72 h campaignAt starts campaign n+1 from the opening map, with no winner computed or shown unless `over` happened.
rootCauses.evidence: Simulated, 60 campaigns per war (nobody playing): 7.5 / 8.6 / 9.4 changes per campaign; first change at 13.6 / 11.8 / 11.2 h on average (min 5.2 h, max 34.4 h); longest quiet spell 22.3 / 19.7 / 18.3 h on average, max 52.0 / 58.6 / 34.6 h. Liberator net swing over a campaign ranges -9 to +9, which is seed luck. WarCard.jsx:53 is the only result line (and only when `over`). gcw.js:156-161, 244.

rootCauses.title: A side can be wiped out, after which the war idles
rootCauses.mechanism: No floor or last stand. A side reduced to 0 systems can't attack (attackOn needs a border, gcw.js:224-225), or, for the liberator, has no fronts (frontsOf). The war is `over` only when liberator or raider owns all 16 (gcw.js:304-305), so a Hutt world left standing keeps a decided war running for hours at Hutt-halved rates. The Remnant War opens 10 against 4, so the Remnant and the Hutts go first.
rootCauses.evidence: Nobody playing: the Remnant is eliminated in 6/60 campaigns (at 24, 34, 35, 42, 53 and 55 h) and the Hutts in 14/60 (from 26 h). The New Republic wins outright in 3/60 (41.4, 43.0, 51.2 h). Clone c0: the Separatists hit 0 at about 63 h, the war stays 15/0/1 until 72 h with one front on Nevarro at 1.7 %/h effective. sides.js:55.

rootCauses.title: Player points are uncapped in effect, count anywhere, and swamp the AI
rootCauses.mechanism: pointsOf adds each side's points/100 plus a win of 0.10 at every system in every step, battle or not. A typical battle (about 15 points plus a win) is 0.25 of a system's hold per 12 minutes, about 1.25 systems an hour, against the AI's 0.02-0.12 an hour. CAP=60 lets one pilot do 0.7 a step. The ground assault posts points whether or not a battle is on there, and taker = the side with the most points flips even a quiet system.
rootCauses.evidence: gcw.js:250-258, 278-292; warState.js:27; GalaxySurface.jsx:369-375. Simulated with one liberator pilot (15 points plus a win per battle at the major order): 3 h a day ends the war outright in 15/30 (Clone Wars), 13/30 (Civil War) and 26/30 (Remnant War) campaigns, with the Remnant war over as early as 30.6 h and the Remnant wiped out as early as 19 h. Playing all day ends every war in 11-15 / 12-15 / 7-9 h. One raider pilot 3 h a day: Civil War over for the Empire at 44.8 h in one campaign.

rootCauses.title: The map's liberation arc and order bar are hard-coded to the Civil War's colours, and their meaning flips
rootCauses.mechanism: galaxy.css sets the liberation arc and track and the major-order bar to Rebel red and Empire green whatever the war, so the Clone Wars and Remnant War maps draw red over green. progressOf is liberated share for a front but held share for an attack (warText.js:27), drawn in the same red, so a full red ring means opposite things.
rootCauses.evidence: galaxy.css:531-532 (`stroke: rgb(98 224 138 / 0.35)`, `stroke: #ff6b4a`), 560-561; HoloMap.jsx:240-242 sets no colour; warText.js:27.

rootCauses.title: The map hides the war's real graph and shows almost no territory
rootCauses.mechanism: Ownership is only a 2 px ring round a 14 px dot filled with the system's own accent colour. The map draws the 6 trade routes, but the war advances along NEIGHBOURS, 28 edges of which only 10 are on drawn routes. Lothal's three neighbours (Kamino, Kashyyyk, Scarif) are all off-route, so it looks cut off. Attacks don't record where they come from (attackOn returns sys, by, from-time, until, rate), so nothing can draw an arrow. The Empire and the Hutts are both green.
rootCauses.evidence: galaxy.css:353-359, 526-527; HoloMap.jsx:229-233; gcw.js:90-112, 236; scratch edges.mjs: the 18 edges not on routes are geonosis-tatooine, kamino-tatooine, naboo-tatooine, endor-hoth, hoth-mustafar, hoth-nevarro, hoth-sorgan, endor-sorgan, kashyyyk-yavin, mandalore-yavin, coruscant-kashyyyk, coruscant-mandalore, coruscant-naboo, geonosis-naboo, kashyyyk-lothal, geonosis-kamino, kamino-lothal, lothal-scarif; sides.js:23, 26.

rootCauses.title: The rate shown isn't the rate that applies
rootCauses.mechanism: warTable's row.rate is the seeded base rate (gcw.js:386). The effective rate adds supply and area bonus and is halved against the Hutts (gcw.js:286). standing() prints row.rate as '+x%/h'.
rootCauses.evidence: gcw.js:286, 386; warText.js:34. For example Tatooine (Hutt) in Clone c1 shows +4.8 %/h but falls at about 2.4 %/h plus supply.

rootCauses.title: mine() is O(wins × history), runs every second on the holotable, and judges the major order on an AI-only replay
rootCauses.mechanism: For each won battle, mine() calls history(war, n, thatStep) with the default value () => 0 until it finds the major. HoloMap's useMemo depends on `now`, so it reruns every second. The no-player replay can name a different major than the real war's, so the gcwMajor achievement can be wrong.
rootCauses.evidence: warState.js:132-136; HoloMap.jsx:137; Galaxy.jsx:309. Measured: mine() takes 423.9 ms with 40 wins, none at the major. warNow takes 21.6 ms, history 15-18 ms at the end of a campaign with a 1,474-key tally, recomputed each second (warState.js:100-103).

rootCauses.title: Choosing which war to view changes the war you fight in
rootCauses.mechanism: The WarCard war tabs call onTheatre → setTheatre, which changes allegiance.war. That drives which war's battles, garrisons and escorts the scene uses (scene.js:257, effectsFor). There is no view-only war filter.

proposals.title: Fix the war's colours and arc meaning on the map
proposals.description: galaxy.css:531-532 and 560-561: replace the hard-coded colours with custom properties. HoloMap.jsx:240 sets style={{'--by': SIDES[r.attack ? r.attack.by : WARS[war].liberator].colour, '--held': heldColour(r.owner)}} on the <g>. The arc strokes var(--by) and the track var(--held); WarCard.jsx:55 sets --by and --held on .holomap-order. For an attack, draw the holder's ring draining (attack: stroke var(--held), dasharray = control); for a front, the liberator's arc filling. Add a small '−' or '+' glyph so a full ring reads unambiguously. sides.js:26: move the Hutts off green, to violet (#b98ae6 or similar), which no other side uses in any war. In warText.standing (warText.js:34), print the effective rate: add `effRate` to warTable rows (gcw.js:386) = pressureOn(owner, rate + supplyOf + areaBonusOf).
proposals.tests: sides.test.js: within each war, the hue distance between liberator, raider and hutt colours is at least 30° (RGB → HSL helper in the test). gcw.test.js: warTable rows on a Hutt front have effRate === rate*GCW.hutts + supply terms. warText.test.js: standing shows effRate when present.

proposals.title: Make mine() one pass, keyed to the tally version, and judge the major on the real war
proposals.description: history(): collect `majors` (fronts[0] per step, an array of length step+1; or run-length [[k, sys]]) in the loop at gcw.js:275, and return it as an additive field. warState.mine(): call history(war, n, now, (k) => t.value(k)) once and read majors[b.step] (warState.js:132-136), instead of one AI-only history per win. Memoise mine on (war, n, version) in warState. HoloMap.jsx:137 depends on warVersion(), not `now`. Galaxy.jsx:98-115 can stay every 5 s since it's cached.
proposals.tests: warState.test.js 'knows a win at the major order' (line 119) still passes. New: with 40 wins, mine() calls history at most once (vi.spyOn on the module export, or count via an injected history). New: a win at a system that is the major only because of player captures counts as major (build a tally where the players' capture changes fronts[0]).

proposals.title: Have history() return events, snapshots, strength and phase (the data the new map needs)
proposals.description: Purely additive output from gcw.js history: `events: [{k, at: start+k*step, type: 'captured'|'repelled'|'attack'|'raid'|'area'|'lastStand'|'phase'|'capital', sys, by, from}]`. Push 'captured' at gcw.js:293, 'attack'/'raid' at 269/273, 'repelled' in the 299-302 filter, and 'area' when areaHolders changes. Cap at the last 64. Add `counts: [{k, [side]: n, worth: {side: Σworth}}]` sampled every 30 steps (6 h) and at the last step. warTable passes them through and adds `strength: {[side]: {systems, worth, share, trend6h}}`. Give each attack an origin: in attackOn (gcw.js:223-237) pick `from` = the attacker's neighbour of sys with the highest control, ties broken by id (deterministic). Return it as `origin`, because `from` is already the start time. New warText functions: eventLine(e, now, side) gives 'Hoth fell to the Empire · 2h ago' or 'The Rebellion held Yavin'; strengthLine(table, side); phaseLine.
proposals.tests: gcw.test.js: the number of 'captured' events equals the number of owner changes, checked by replaying history at every step for one campaign. Events are identical across two calls. Each attack has an origin that borders sys and is owned by `by`. counts at k=0 equal opening counts; Σ over sides = 16. warText.test.js: eventLine wording for each type and the 'ago' spans.

proposals.title: Strategic AI v2, part 1: no stalls (dynamic rates, defence, regeneration, rotation)
proposals.description: In gcw.js (pure; numbers from the prototype). (a) Re-roll each front's rate every 30 steps (6 h) from seeded(`gcw-${war}-${n}-${id}-${Math.floor(k/30)}`), with GCW.rate [2,11] and majorRate [1,8]. Precompute all 12 windows in campaignPlan so they aren't re-seeded per step. (b) The holder's own fleets push back at a front: subtract GCW.defence = 1 %/h, or 0.3 × that if the system is cut off. (c) A system nobody is attacking and that is in supply regains GCW.regen = 4 %/h up to 1. This replaces the permanent dents and makes the Hutt vulture deliberate rather than accidental. (d) A captured system starts at GCW.captured = 0.7, and a repelled attack restores +0.25, not to 1. (e) Stall rotation: a front other than fronts[0] that lost less than 0.1 hold in 30 steps is rested for 30 steps, so the next candidate takes its slot. All of this is loop-local state derived from (war, n, k, owner, control, tally), so every pilot computes the same.
proposals.tests: Major order stuck (effective AI rate <= 0.5 %/h) under 10% of steps over 20 campaigns; the prototype measured 0-1%. No 24 h window without an ownership change over 20 campaigns. A system with no attack or front regains control at GCW.regen. Rates differ between windows 0 and 1 for some system. Tests to update: 'gives a front to the liberator, whole' and 'gives back one held to the end whole' (gcw.test.js:226-253) now expect GCW.captured, or control >= the previous value plus GCW.repelled.

proposals.title: Strategic AI v2, part 2: smart targets, faction doctrine, counter-attacks
proposals.description: Replace the weight-random pick in attackOn (gcw.js:223-237) with argmax of a seeded utility. For a border candidate c attacked by `by` at rate r: u = worth(c)·d.worth + (1−control[c])·2·d.weak + cutOff(c)·d.cut + areaWhole(c, by)·2·d.area + weight(c)·0.5 + (counter target ? 6 : 0) + (expected fall pressureOn(holder, r+supply+area)·hours/100 ≥ 0.8·control[c] ? 2 : −4) − (attacked within the last 60 steps ? 3 : 0) + rand()·d.jitter. Here cutOff is the number of the holder's systems that would lose their path to its capital, and areaWhole is 1 if taking c completes an area for `by`. Add a DOCTRINE table, data only, in sides.js: republic {worth 3, weak 1, cut 1, area 1, jitter 1}, separatists {1, 2, 1, 0.5, 1.5, every 0.8}, rebel {1, 3, 0.5, 1, 1.5}, empire {3, 1, 2, 1, 0.5}, newrepublic {2, 1, 1, 2, 1}, remnant {3, 2, 1, 0, 1, every 0.9}, hutt {0.5, 4, 0, 0, 1}. Counter-attacks: when a main side loses a system, record counter[side] = {sys, until: k+10}. The raider launches its next attack on it at once if it has none running; the liberator puts it at fronts[0] with +6 %/h. The Hutts don't counter. Keep the attack due at k=20 (the test at attackEvery+60s), but open with a strike at k=5 so day 1 moves. Prototype attack ranges: attackRate [25,62], raidRate [12,30].
proposals.tests: Over 20 campaigns, under 10% of raider attacks are on Hutt worlds they couldn't take. Counter: after a scripted capture (player points), the losing side's next operation targets that system within 10 steps. With doctrine weights forced on a crafted owner map, the attack picks the expected system. Determinism: same output twice. Tests to keep: 'sends the raider against a border system every so often' (gcw.test.js:148-158); 'the Hutts raid' and 'can take' (159-187). The scratch prototype run keeps the Hutts taking and losing worlds.

proposals.title: Strategic AI v2, part 3: campaign phases, last stand, climax, victory points
proposals.description: GCW.phases = [{from: 0, name: 'Opening', mult: 0.9, every: 15}, {from: 60, name: 'Escalation', mult: 1.0, every: 20}, {from: 240, name: 'Decisive', mult: 1.1, every: 18}, {from: 330, name: 'Climax', mult: 1.3, every: 12}], with from and every in steps. mult scales every AI rate; every is the raider's cadence, scaled by doctrine.every. Underdog boost: a side holding under 30% of the systems gets ×1.35 on its rates, one over 60% gets ×0.8. Last stand: before the Climax, a side's last GCW.lastStand = 1 system can't fall below 0.02 control, so no faction (Hutts included) is eliminated before 66 h. Climax: fronts[0] gets ×2 and the decisive battle is flagged (warTable `decisive: sys`). `over` can then only happen in the Climax. At the end, warTable.result = {winner by VP (Σ worth held), vp: {side: n}, decisive}. Return `phase` and `nextOp: {by, at}` for the countdowns. Measured in the prototype (40 campaigns, nobody playing): Civil War 7.2/6.1/2.8, Clone Wars 7.0/6.8/2.1, Remnant War 9.1/5.3/1.6; no eliminations or early ends before 66 h; about 29-33 changes per campaign, roughly twice as many on day 3 as day 1. One pilot 3 h a day: Civil War 10.7/3.8, ended only in the Climax (1/30). Grinding all day: ends at 66-70 h, not 7-15 h.
proposals.tests: No side reaches 0 systems before step 330 in 20 campaigns × 3 wars × {no players, a liberator grinding every step with 100 points}. result.winner is the VP argmax. phase names by step. Test to update: 'ends a war early when one side holds every system' (gcw.test.js:286-292) moves to at(0, 70*H). Add a slow gcw.scenario.test.js (left out of npm test by vite.config.js:19) that asserts the balance bands: liberator final share within ±25% of opening on average, attack success 30-60%, at least 12 changes per campaign.

proposals.title: Strategic AI v2, part 4: supply lines and capitals
proposals.description: Add WARS[war].capitals in sides.js: clone {republic: 'coruscant', separatists: 'geonosis'}, gcw {rebel: 'yavin', empire: 'coruscant'}, remnant {newrepublic: 'coruscant', remnant: 'mandalore'}, and hutt: 'tatooine' in all. In gcw.js, supplied(owner, side) is a BFS from the capital through the side's own systems (from its worthiest system if the capital has fallen). Recompute it only on steps where an owner changed, which keeps the cost down. A cut-off system gets no regeneration and 0.3× defence, and makes an easy target (part 2's cutOff utility). Capital lost → a 'capital' event, and its side's rates drop to 0.85× for 30 steps (shock). Keep supplyOf (gcw.js:176-180) unchanged as the local term, so its exact test (gcw.test.js:313-318) holds.
proposals.tests: supplied() on crafted owner maps: an encircled system is excluded. A cut-off system's control doesn't regenerate. Losing the capital emits a 'capital' event once. sides.test.js: each capital is in its side's opening.

proposals.title: Bound and localise player influence
proposals.description: In history's pointsOf use (gcw.js:250-258, 278-282): (a) Count a side's points only where there is a battle that step (front or attack), or at the side's own systems (defence). Elsewhere drop them, which closes the ground-assault backdoor; also gate GalaxySurface.jsx:369-375 on battleAt(...) != null or own system. (b) Soft cap per side per system per step: eff = min(GCW.playerCap, min(p, GCW.knee) + max(0, p − GCW.knee)·0.35), with knee 0.3 and playerCap 0.45. This keeps the exact-arithmetic tests (0.2, 0.3−0.1, the 0.1 win) valid. With AI v2's last stand, defence and regeneration, the prototype held a lone grinder to a Climax-only end. If the owner wants a lone pilot weaker, knee 0.1 (measured: 3 h/day gives Civil War 9.9/4.4).
proposals.tests: Points at a quiet enemy system (no front or attack that step) don't change its control. 1000 points in one step move control by at most playerCap. The existing 'takes a front's hold down' (−0.2), 'the holder's pilots push back' (+0.1) and 'counts a battle won once' tests stay green. Rewrite 'gives a front to the liberator, whole' to spread 100 points over 3 steps.

proposals.title: Map, territory layer: capped Voronoi cells, front lines, contested links
proposals.description: New pure module src/components/galaxy/territory.js: cellsOf(systems, {rim: RIM, core: CORE, cap: (s) => 1.1 + 0.35*worth}) clips a 24-gon of radius cap round each system by the perpendicular bisector half-planes against every other war system (Sutherland–Hodgman, n = 16), then by the disc. Each new edge is tagged with the neighbour whose bisector made it, giving {id, poly: [[x, z]...], edges: [{with, a, b}]}. It is computed once at module load (positions are static). Closest pairs: Hoth–Bespin 0.57, Tatooine–Geonosis 0.64. bordersOf(cells, owner) gives the edges whose two cells have different owners. linksOf(table) = NEIGHBOURS edges with state 'own' (same owner), 'contested' (different owners) or 'battle' (either end has row.battle). Draw in HoloMap.jsx's SVG after the grid and before the regions: cells filled color-mix(var(--held) 10-22%, scaled by control). A cell under attack or a front gets an SVG <pattern> hatch in the attacker's colour. Borders are a white line with glow, animated dash when either side is fighting (reuse holomap-dash). War links are drawn over the routes (dim the routes to 0.18): own in the owner's colour at 0.25, contested dashed white, battle animated. All aria-hidden, and animations off under prefers-reduced-motion (galaxy.css:569-572).
proposals.tests: territory.test.js: every system lies inside its own cell. 2000 seeded random points in the disc each fall in the cell of their nearest capped system or in none. No two cells overlap (sampled). Each border edge's midpoint is equidistant (±1e-6) from its two systems. linksOf returns exactly the 28 NEIGHBOURS edges with the right states on a crafted table. Snapshot the cell count (16).

proposals.title: Map, operations and fleets: arrows and moving fleet tokens
proposals.description: A pure warMap.js: opsOf(table) gives [{by, from: origin system (gcw part 3 `origin`) or, for a front, the liberator's neighbour with the highest control, to, kind: 'front'|'attack'|'raid'|'counter'|'decisive', progress: progressOf(row), colour: SIDES[by].colour, width: 0.05 + 0.004·|effRate|}]. HoloMap draws each as a path with a marker arrowhead and a flowing dash (raids dotted, the decisive battle double). It draws a fleet token (an SVG <symbol> per side in emblems.js: simple geometric crests, not studio logos) at lerp(from, to, 0.35 + 0.5·progress), so the fleet visibly closes in as liberation proceeds. Tokens for idle sides are optional (one at the capital).
proposals.tests: opsOf on warTable(…) at several moments: one op per front or attack; from borders to (NEIGHBOURS) and is owned by `by`; progress in [0,1]; the colour is the side's. emblems.js has a symbol for every SIDES id.

proposals.title: Map, panels: faction strength, event feed, phase and countdowns, view tabs, legend, your part, join
proposals.description: (1) Faction strip over the map (HTML, top-left): per side an emblem, '9 systems · 41% of the galaxy's worth', and a ▲/▼ for the last 6 h from table.strength; a stacked bar liberator | Hutts | raider. (2) Event feed in WarCard: the last 6 table.events via warText.eventLine, each clickable (setPick), aria-live polite. Events newer than this viewer's last look are highlighted; keep `tp-gcw-seen` {war: k} in localStorage as a per-viewer convenience, wrapped in try/catch. (3) WarCard.jsx:51 kicker: 'Escalation · climax in 18h · campaign ends in 2d 3h', plus 'Next Imperial offensive in 47m' from table.nextOp. (4) A view-only war switch: HoloMap keeps `view` state (default oath.war) driving warNow(now, view). Tabs switch view; a separate 'Fight in this war' button calls onTheatre. (5) A legend toggle covering territory, front line, link states, arrow, fleet, battle on, decisive, major order. (6) Your part: 'You moved Hoth 14% this campaign', from mine().systems and soft-capped shares, plus a dot on systems where you fought. (7) A 'Join the nearest battle' button: of the battles where your side is attacker or defender, the one with the shortest jumpSeconds from `current`, calling onGo. (8) A campaign result card when table.result or over: 'The Empire won campaign 7 · 38–31 · decisive at Coruscant'. (9) Major order as an order with a deadline: gcw picks orders[side] = {sys, verb: 'liberate'|'hold'|'take', from, until} at 30-step boundaries (or when completed or failed), so it doesn't flicker. The prototype's fronts[0] changed every 2.5 h.
proposals.tests: warText.test.js: strengthLine, phaseLine, eventLine and resultLine strings. gcw.test.js: orders[side] stays the same within a 30-step window unless captured, the liberator's order is a front, and the raider's order is its attack or one of its systems under threat. WarCard: pure helpers only (nearestBattle(table, current, side) is tested in warText or warMap).

proposals.title: Cost control for the per-second replay
proposals.description: AI v2 done naively costs 54 ms per full replay against 15 ms now (scratch perf3.mjs), and warNow replays every second (warState.js:100-103). (a) In campaignPlan, precompute the rate windows and seeded streams. (b) Run the supply BFS only on steps where an owner changed. (c) In warState, memoise the state at the last whole step per (war, n, version, last): export a historyUpTo(war, n, k, value) plus a partial(state, frac), or let history take an optional cache object. warNow then applies only the current step's fraction each second, and replays in full only when the tally version or step changes. Keep history() itself pure and exported unchanged.
proposals.tests: gcw.test.js: the cached path equals the uncached history (toEqual) at 20 random moments with a busy tally. A timing guard (loose, under 25 ms in Node) on a full-campaign history with a 1,500-key tally.

constraints: Online determinism: history(war, n, ms, value) and warTable must remain pure functions of (war, campaign n, wall-clock ms, tally values). No Date.now, Math.random or module state that changes results (the planOf cache at gcw.js:209-217 is fine). All randomness goes through seeded(`gcw-${war}-${n}-…`) (gcw.js:120-129). Loop-local AI memory (counters, stall marks, next-op steps) is fine because it is re-derived on every replay.

The tally is the only shared state. Keep pointsKey/winKey formats and readKey (including the old `hoth:12` Rebellion keys, gcw.js:134-154). Any new key must match tally.js's KEY regex /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9:._-]{0,47}$/ and counts against warState KEYS = 23040 (warState.js:29). Every pilot's history must agree once tallies converge (gcw.test.js:254-285).

battleAt's id `${epoch}.${war}.${sys}.${step}` and seed = hash(id) (gcw.js:341, 350) key the battle's shared fight tally in warfront.js, and teamsOf (light side 0, dark 1, Hutts in the other's place) pins teams. Don't change these, GCW.step or GCW.fight, or start/fightEnd/end.

Changing GCW.start, GCW.campaign or GCW.step renumbers campaigns and steps, which breaks saved tallies (epoch c{n}, warState.js:58-70) and the allegiance `since` (allegiance.js:36). Change them only at a campaign boundary, or not at all.

warTable row shape is read by HoloMap, WarCard, warText, warEffects (heat from row.attack/front, warEffects.js:74), GalaxyPanel, WarHud, Galaxy.jsx, GalaxySurface and scene.js:257. Changes must be additive: owner ∈ {liberator, raider, hutt}; control in [0,1]; rate a number on fronts; battle non-null for every front and attack (gcw.test.js:384-407). history's return is used by warfront.js:240 (fronts, attacks, owner, war for battleAt).

Tests that pin current behaviour and would need deliberate edits under AI v2: the fronts worth-ordered with major = fronts[0] at 30 min (gcw.test.js:106-120); exact control deltas −0.2, +0.1 and win/100 (188-225); capture leaves control 1 (226-233); an attack held to the end leaves control 1 and a 30-point save works (234-253); early end at 30 h (286-292); the supply formula (313-318); the raider attack present at attackEvery + 60 s (148-158); a Hutt raid at raidEvery + 60 s within 6 campaigns (159-172); Hutts both taking and losing worlds within 20 campaigns (173-187); 'moves both ways' within 6 campaigns (131-147). warState.test 'knows a win at the major order' (line 119).

Performance budget: warNow replays the whole campaign every second on the main thread (about 15-22 ms now at a campaign's end). Any AI v2 must stay about this cost per full replay, or add the step-checkpoint cache. Slow balance simulations belong in *.scenario.test.js, which vite.config.js:19 keeps out of npm test.

House style: pure rules modules with Vitest tests first (gcw.js, warText.js, a new territory.js/warMap.js), data in sides.js/systems.js, prose comments in the files' voice, and drawing last in HoloMap.jsx/galaxy.css. SVG layers aria-hidden, systems stay focusable buttons with aria-labels, animations off under prefers-reduced-motion (galaxy.css:569-572).

This investigation was read-only: no tracked file was edited and nothing was committed. Scratch scripts are under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-new-portfolio-website/388c0198-4eb1-51a0-b00a-e0c292df4509/scratchpad/warmap/ (run with `node --import ./register.mjs <script>` from that directory). No browser check was run, because this area didn't call for one.
openQuestions: Should a war still be able to end early (the spec's `over`, and the test at 30 h), or only in the Climax phase? The last stand needs the latter.

Should a captured system come in at 0.7 hold, and a repelled attack restore only partly? Both remove the 'whole again' wording and tests (gcw.test.js:226-253); the alternative is to keep 1 and rely on regeneration and defence for back-and-forth.

Campaign carry-over: the tally resets every epoch (warState.js:58-70), so a newcomer can't recompute the previous campaign's true result. Should results be display-only and kept per browser, or should the next opening shift by an AI-only previous result that everyone can compute?

How strong should one pilot be? knee 0.3 keeps the current tests and lets a 3 h/day pilot swing about 5 systems; knee 0.1 halves that. With few visitors online, the site may want one person's play to matter visibly.
Is the Hutts' colour change acceptable? SIDES.colour also tints battles (battles.js:230). Should emblems be simple stand-in crests (recommended) or the films' insignia?
Should the major order become a per-side order with a 6 h deadline (Helldivers-style), or stay 'the liberator's top front'? WarCard's 'Hold/Liberate' wording (WarCard.jsx:58) depends on it.
The docs disagree with the code: the spec says supply 1 and regionBonus 2, the code has supply 0.5 and areaBonus 1 (gcw.js:67-68); sides.js:72 still says regionBonus. Which values are intended?
Keep the 72 h campaign? The prototype's phases make 72 h work, but most visits are minutes long. Highlighting what happened since the last visit (tp-gcw-seen) matters more than the campaign's length.
